quest.title: The Night the Moon Returns Home
quest.description: The Moon-Prayer Night has come. On this final night, what memories will she leave behind?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1500, Mora x66000, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x12

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act VI
chapter.title: Melting Moonlight in the Morning Mist

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Wow. The Frostmoon Scions' stall looks kinda plain, but it's pretty cool once you get into it.)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (I don't go to Hiisi Island much, but it's got that, like... "olde worlde" cultural feel.)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Heh, and if culture means we get more festivals, I'm all for it!)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hello, Jahoda.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Whoa! Columbin— Uhh, hello, Moon Goddess!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (That was too close! I almost gave the game away in front of the staff! ...Wait, what's the deal with her shoes? They don't make a sound when she walks! I could do with a pair of those...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Do you like balloons too?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Balloons? Oh... you mean those.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (What's so fun about balloons? I'm not a kid anymore... They're probably more up Aino's alley.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. The animals seem very curious about these strange flying objects. I was drawn here by their voices.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I recently learned a fun new game you can play with balloons, so I decided to come and give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: A new game...?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hello.

dialogues.speaker: Reetta
dialogues.text: Ah, welcome home, Moon Goddess. Here to buy some balloons?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. Could you give me a few that haven't been inflated yet?

dialogues.speaker: Reetta
dialogues.text: Hmm? Are you sure? ...I guess it's not a problem, but...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes please. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Uninflated balloons? But those are just... little rubber pouches. What does she want with those?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Would you like to play the balloon game, Jahoda?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Huh? Uh, sure, I guess? How do you play it...?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Wait here a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Ugh... This is so weird. What have I gotten myself into now?)

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Hmm? I thought I saw Columbina nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Uh-oh! That's... The Fourth Harbinger! ...Although, she's helped us out quite a bit. She's good people, right?)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Is she looking for Columbina? Phew. Guess that's my ticket out of here. I'm not sure my heart can take being sandwiched between two Harbingers!)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Which stall is she checking out? Oh, it's that other Frostmoon Scions one — try on the headgear, see what it's like having antlers or animal ears for a day.)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (I wouldn't be caught dead wearing that stuff... So embarrassing. I have enough gear to carry as it is...)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Wait, what!? She put it on!?)

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: (...How peculiar. This would take some getting used to... I wonder if this is what it's like for Lynette?)

dialogues.speaker: Zirnytsia
dialogues.text: It really suits you, Ma'am.

dialogues.speaker: Zirnytsia
dialogues.text: (What is this? She was so intimidating a moment ago, but now... Dang, she's really rockin' those ears! How does she make 'em look so cool?)

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: (Hmph... I suppose I may as well keep them on for now. All part of the festive experience.)

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (She's coming this way!)

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: How do you do, Miss Jahoda?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Oh geez, don't talk to me while wearing that thing! Where am I supposed to look!?)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... Hey there.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: I'm looking for Columbina. Have you seen her?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Ah, sh—she, she just... Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (W—W—Wait, is THAT what she meant by "balloon game"—)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Hyah!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: No fair, how come I get caught in the crossfire!?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: An ambush from the rear? Is this a declaration of war, Columbina?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Would you like to play too, Arlecchino?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Seriously!? Are they gonna start some beef right here, right now?)

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Gladly. That said, I believe there is another who would like to join.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...! Boss! Boss Nef! Thank goodness! You've gotta get me outta here, things are kicking off big time!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hello there. I'd like ten... No, make that twenty balloons, please. Uninflated.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Miss Moon Goddess, I hope you're prepared to pay the price for assaulting my employee?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Haha. Welcome to the game, Nefer.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Just to be clear, let's keep this a fair fight, okay? No strange powers, please and thank you.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Naturally.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hmm? Don't just stand there, Jahoda — aren't you going to team up with me?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Huh? Do I have to?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Of course. Don't forget, the Curatorium has a reputation to uphold.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...I knew something like this was gonna happen!

dialogues.speaker: Zirnytsia
dialogues.text: Welcome home, Moon Goddess. Would you like to try on some animal-themed headwear?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Ah... I always hear Lauma saying how heavy her antlers are. I wonder how it feels?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Let me give it a try...)

dialogues.speaker: Zirnytsia
dialogues.text: Oh my, it really suits you!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (It's a little itchy, and it's hard to turn my head...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Should I keep wearing it?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I'll keep it on.

dialogues.speaker: Zirnytsia
dialogues.text: Alright! Feel free to come back if you change your mind!

dialogues.speaker: Kaarina
dialogues.text: ...Sunny days! I prefer sunny days!

dialogues.speaker: A Talking Magic Lamp (?)
dialogues.text: Aw, well you are as warm as the sun itself, Moon Goddess.

dialogues.speaker: A Talking Magic Lamp (?)
dialogues.text: Very well, I believe your spirit animal has to be...

dialogues.speaker: A Talking Magic Lamp (?)
dialogues.text: ...This most adorable Chic Badger.

dialogues.speaker: Kaarina
dialogues.text: Wow! Thank you, Mister Talking Magic Lamp!

dialogues.speaker: A Talking Magic Lamp (?)
dialogues.text: Haha. Have a very happy festival, Moon Goddess.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Flins? That's you, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: #Shh. It's our little secret, my dear {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Okay, sure, but... Why are you here selling sugar sculptures?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Everyone celebrates in their own way. After gazing into the Abyss and spending time around gravestones all year, what better way to relax than to see sunny smiles on the faces of the living?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Besides that, I like to think of myself as a fair judge of character. I daresay matching personalities to confections suits me rather well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's not what Paimon was talking about! Aren't you afraid that your true identity might be exposed?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hmm? Should I be? There is all manner of magic in the air this Moon-Prayer Night, thanks to the work of the great mages.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I see Miss Columbina is hiding in plain sight — why should I not do the same? Why miss this rare opportunity to enjoy a special evening in my true form?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fair enough, you've got a point there. People who don't know you will probably think you're just a talking lantern.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Haha... Well, now that we see eye to eye, what brings you here? Not a search for your spirit animal, I presume?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, well actually... Here, see for yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Oh, this is... how wonderful. A beautiful idea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. We just met Varka, and he said that having everyone draw their own section was kinda boring... so he did your bit for you.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Haha... Ah, Varka. Ever the maverick. I see his artistic skills are... truly one of a kind.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: In that case, I shall paint something on Mr. Albedo's behalf in a short while.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Why not now?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: ...Ahem. Welcome home, Moon Goddess.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (...! That was close...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hello, Flins.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...She recognized you right away!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Haha, what keen eyes you have, Miss Columbina... Um, especially considering they are shut.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I did not see you. Rather, I sensed you. I can sense the fluctuations in kuuvahki all around me.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: One would expect no less of the Moon Goddess. Might I interest you in some candy?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes, please.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Excellent, I shall make some for you right away.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Something the matter, Miss Columbina?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...What about my "spirit animal"? All the other children carrying sugar sculptures are talking about it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Wait, is she taking the test seriously?)

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Ah, my apologies. How could I neglect that?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: You are quite right, Miss Columbina. Every one of us has a magical creature living in their heart. Would you permit me to help you find yours?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes, please.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: ...Do you prefer the day, or the night?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Night.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Which of the four seasons is your favorite?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Winter.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Think of a perfect day. What is the weather like? Sunny? Rainy? Or perhaps, cloudy?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Rainy in the morning, sunny at night.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (...What kind of answer is that!?)

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Forests, lakes, and open seas — which do you prefer of these?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I like them all.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Imagine you opened your very own shop. What would you sell there?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm... Moonlight, I think.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Wow. Paimon would totally shop there.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How much would it sell for?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It wouldn't cost anything. You'd just need to visit.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Aha. I believe I know what your spirit animal is...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Here. For you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, it's a kuuhenki!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Indeed. A free-spirited being with a deep love for all things here in Nod-Krai, who selflessly lends her aid to as many people as she can reach.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: It is the perfect fit for you, Miss Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Heh. Thank you.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: #Haha. It would be my honor, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: But you shall have to forgive me. We have known each other for quite some time... I doubt there is any answer I could give that would come as a surprise to you.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: So, instead... would you accept this sugar sculpture as a token of our friendship?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: It's a lantern...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Heyyy, uh, why don't you two go enjoy your candy over there? Paimon wants to try out this "spirit animal" thing too! Right, Flins?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (C'mon, play ball, gotta get this drawing done!)

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: But I want to hear Paimon's answers...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah! But... it'll probably take ages! Paimon's a... complex soul! Uhh... And we don't want your candy to melt while you wait, huh?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Oh... Okay then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Phew...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Nice excuse, Lady Paimon. That was some quick thinking.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, no thanks to you! A little help next time?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: #(It's sweet... Is that... Lakkaberry? I wonder what flavor {NICKNAME} got...)

response.speaker: Kaarina
response.text: This way, this way! It's the candy-selling lantern!

response.speaker: Lemetti
response.text: I'm coming!

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: (Ah! Of course...)

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, maybe we can share?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Share?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Yes. I found out recently that people share their food sometimes, so I'd like to try it. Or... is that a no?

choices.text: Oh, no, we can do that...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Hmm... Yours is a little more sour than mine. Here, you try it.

choices.text: I'll just have a little nibble...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Are you sure?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Haha... Amazing...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What is?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: My sugar sculpture has shrunk, yet my heart is filled with feelings of sweetness.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: ...I will remember this feeling.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Would you like another bite?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Sure.

choices.text: Just, uh, don't take too big of a bite...
Now I wanna give this a try...

dialogues.speaker: Katya
dialogues.text: "I wish for a never-ending supply of Lakkaberries..."

dialogues.speaker: Katya
dialogues.text: What a humble wish. Probably written by a child...

dialogues.speaker: Katya
dialogues.text: Hmm? Is that Lauma the Moonchanter...?

dialogues.speaker: Katya
dialogues.text: "I wish that the Longplume Ibises would stop biting me..."

dialogues.speaker: Katya
dialogues.text: Oh dear. Poor Lauma...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Alright. I'll write that one down for you.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. I got it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: While everyone else is celebrating Moon-Prayer Night, you're as busy as ever...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I don't mind. It's rewarding work. A good kind of busy.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: My antlers are at their heaviest tonight, and the kuuvahki waves are especially strong...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But as I help these dear friends hang their wishes up, I feel a great peace within myself that is hard to describe.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: You see? They are all such beautiful wishes.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...And they are ones that we can fulfill by our own strength.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Do you blame me, Lauma? I want to hear your honest answer.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It is by the help of so many people that I can return to the moon... But I feel as though I've hardly done anything in return.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: You've done plenty, Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I say this in earnest, both as someone who knows your history... and also as a friend, who has seen what you've been through.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: What about as a Moonchanter?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Hah... I feel proud to honor our Moon Goddess's wish, and I'm sure any Moonchanter in history would have felt the same way.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Thank you for your kind words, Lauma.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...Since you asked for my honesty, I won't lie to you. My feelings are mixed right now. Besides pride, I also feel...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I suppose it's... a reluctance to let go.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Once you return to the moon, we will be far apart, and separated by a false sky.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I'm sure those of us left behind will gaze up at that sky, yearning for the moon once in a while... just as you used to do.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I will miss you, Lauma. I will miss you all.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I hope to stay in touch. I will try and find some way to send messages down from the moon.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Perhaps you could use kuuvahki?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I've heard Jahoda say that signals can be sent using long and short waves, or strong and weak lights.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm... That sounds a little complicated. What if we forget what the signals mean?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: We could prepare a codebook beforehand, but... Heh, you're right. It wouldn't really suit you.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Still, whatever happens, I believe that you will find your own unique way of communicating with us.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: And now that I think about that, my heart feels lighter.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Because you trust in me?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Yes, I have faith in you, and in the power of truth.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: In my experience, the truth tends to be difficult. But that's what makes it stand out from what is false.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: So, I'm confident that your thoughts and your love will shine through the curtain of lies. We will know it when we see it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Thank you... Now, could you help me hang up my wish?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Is this...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I wish that all who dwell in this moonlit world can find a place to belong, and I wish that I shall one day see my friends again.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It's two wishes... I hope that's not too greedy of me?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Not at all. And I think you speak for us all with the second one.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I shall continue to pray until the day that all of these wishes come true.

dialogues.speaker: Jacek
dialogues.text: Dodoco's Whirly Gig! Come check out Dodoco's Whirly Gig!

dialogues.speaker: Jacek
dialogues.text: Ah, welcome home, Moon Goddess.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Might I ask what this is?

dialogues.speaker: Jacek
dialogues.text: Ah, it's a very special amusement sponsored by the great mage herself! Ride on a soft and furry Dodoco, and embark on an unforgettable adventure!

dialogues.speaker: Jacek
dialogues.text: (I say that, but I'm just following a script, here... Who is this mage, anyway? And what the heck's a Dodoco?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I'd like to ride.

dialogues.speaker: Jacek
dialogues.text: No problem. But, uh... are you by yourself?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Is that not okay?

dialogues.speaker: Jacek
dialogues.text: Oh, no, it's fine. It's just that each Dodoco can accommodate two passengers. Would you like to bring a friend along?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: My friends...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...That should do it. Now we just need to get everyone else to draw something on it too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we gotta keep it a secret from Columbina...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Um, yes?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I want to go on that ride. Will you join me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (A spinning Dodoco? Ah, I see. It's a ride for two.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Let's go, then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh, one moment!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (...Don't worry! Paimon will do the rounds. You go have fun!)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Thanks, Paimon!)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm...?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Alright. I think we have to wait in line over there...

response.speaker: Jacek
response.text: Please take your seats. For safety reasons, you mustn't try to leave the ride before it comes to a complete stop.

response.speaker: Jacek
response.text: Alright, you're all set! I wish you both a wonderful journey!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (You can always rely on Alice for weird and wonderful gadgets...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What did you think?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Not bad... It reminds me of riding a Moonlane.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Sometimes, the kuuhenki circle around me like this, playing their beautiful melodies.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Aw. That sounds so sweet.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Yeah. I'm going to miss them.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I wonder what Columbina will find on the moon? ...Perhaps even she doesn't know...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Does it... scare you at all?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: ...It does.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I've felt scared in the past, too. But this is a little different.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: ...You know something? I got to see a lot of fascinating things during my "disappearance."

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I saw how the Frostmoon Scions act around their families... so different than how they used to act in my presence. And I also saw how they interact with their friends.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: It made me curious at first. Why do people act so sincere when they're worshiping gods, but save their truest, warmest feelings for each other?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Slowly, I came to realize that... it's because they trust one another. They know, deep down, that they'll be accepted for who they are — all of it, the good and the bad.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Your friends accept all of you, too.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I know. I knew it the moment you started calling out my name.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: What I fear now is the end... I fear losing all this the very night I have gained it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You won't lose us...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Hmm...?

choices.text: Even after you return to the moon...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Thank you for this conversation... Thank you for listening to me.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Don't worry. This fear I have, and the unknown that awaits me — they cannot hurt me. Not when I possess a treasure far greater.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I just... want you to remember this version of me, the real me, on this final night together.

response.speaker: Jacek
response.text: Dear passengers, Dodoco's awesome adventure has come to a close. Please leave in an orderly fashion, and we look forward to seeing you again in the future!

response.speaker: Jacek
response.text: ...Hmm? Don't want the journey to end, huh?

response.speaker: Jacek
response.text: Don't worry, you two. There's always another adventure waiting just around the corner.

choices.text: Your friends will still be here.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Remarkable talent!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: It's not too easy, is it? Still, I'm sure you'll familiarize yourself with Jumpy Dumpty's attack range in no time!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: So, what do you make of it?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The use of Jumpy Dumpties doesn't come as naturally to me as kuuvahki. But their unpredictability makes it fun.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I think they call this... novelty?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Indeed! And how did it feel, blowing those pesky nuisances away?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Not bad.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Any guilt?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Wonderful! Lovely answers to all three questions. You've passed the safety test! Now, I can give this special bomb to you as a souvenir.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Remember, if you find any meanies living on the moon, you can use this to boom them into oblivion!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I will.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...I wouldn't say it's "unfair," exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I mean, your voice goes right into peoples' heads. How would you explain that to the kids?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: You can't just explain it away as magic...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Is something the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ah, Miss Columbina! No, nothing you need to worry yourself about...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Ah, impeccable timing! Stick around for a second, Miss Columbina. I need your input on something.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: This self-proclaimed knight of justice has yet to give me a satisfactory answer. I, for one, would like to hear your verdict on the matter.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ahem... Hey now, I left The Flagship just to help you out, Ms. Nicole...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: So, Alice and I are both using long-range remote control spells that work on similar principles, allowing us to attend this festive fair in Dodoco form...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Sorry, let me backtrack a little — while similar, there are some key differences.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Alice, being a great mage, wanted her Dodoco to reflect something of her own charm and mystique, so she adjusted the way its tail moves when it spins around.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: An entirely gratuitous move, in my opinion. I hardly see how anyone is going to notice that.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: If anything, I'd say that anyone who stares intently enough at a Dodoco's tail to notice such a small detail is someone we ought to be highly concerned about.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I only say this to emphasize that my question has nothing to do with tails. Now that we're clear on that... Why is Alice's Dodoco permitted to interact directly with the children celebrating Moon-Prayer Night, while mine is not?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Your voice speaks directly into people's minds...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: See? Exactly what I said.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ms. Nicole?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Ugh... I can't stand it!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I know, that probably makes me sound like a whiny child acting out in front of their parents... hmm, and it's a little embarrassing now that I think about it...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: But hey, I've said it now. I can't take it back — that would be even more embarrassing!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: ...Also, don't go reading too much into that analogy. It was off the top of my head. I'm actually an awful lot older than either of you...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Ms. Nicole, are you saying that you'd like someone to play the game you've prepared?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Eh, I'm not so invested in that. It's just something cobbled together using items I borrowed from Alice. She probably didn't even make them herself.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: The point is, I want to know everyone's thoughts after they receive their prizes! But as you've said, I can't just ask...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I've been biting my lip for so long! And I've had no one to vent my frustrations on.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: *sigh* I thought this was going to be a nice, straightforward festival where I'd get the chance to guide people to treasure...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Well, can I play? I can't guarantee that I'll win a prize, but...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: You will?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I'd like to try.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Then what are we waiting for? Let the game begin!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: (...It's like they forgot I was ever here. Hahaha.)

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I know, that probably makes me sound like...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: a whiny child acting out in front of their parents...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Hmm, and it's a little embarrassing

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: now that I think about it...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: But hey, I've said it now...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I can't take it back —

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: That would be even more embarrassing!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Congratulations, Miss Columbina! With your great wisdom, you have overcome every obstacle in your path and conquered the great challenge posed to you by Fate.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Fate?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Well, something to that effect. If you'd prefer something more poetic, it could be... "the icy winds," or "the dawn"... anything you like, really.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: ...You could even go with "the challenge posed to you by Dodoco," if that's what you're into. Anyway, you can take or leave my suggestions. Moving on...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: All my hopes are now resting on this.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Can I... open it now?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Stop teasing me! Please, I'm begging you — no more talk, just open it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Wow... What a lovely sculpture. Classic and cute at the same time... Thank you, Ms. Nicole. I'll always treasure it.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Ahhhh, there we go... Music to my ears...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: You have my sincerest gratitude, Miss Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Thank you for sharing your precious time with me and fulfilling my wish.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Don't mention it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You've all done much to help me, and still I'm the one receiving all these gifts...

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Welcome home, Moon Goddess.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Oh? You're the genuine article. Alice was right. This Moon-Prayer Night was worth watching after all.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Another one that talks...

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Greetings, pleased to make your acquaintance. I am the Hexenzirkel member they call "B" — Barbeloth Trismegistus.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Columbina Hyposelenia. Pleased to meet you too.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Hyposelenia... Mm, a fine name indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Now then, Miss Columbina... Do you wish to hear a mage's divination?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Divination... The Frostmoon Scions used to ask me what would happen in the future. Is this like that?

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: From the perspective of the one seeking answers, perhaps.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: As you look to your journey ahead, if you seek to understand the unknown, resolve your doubts, and soothe the confusion in your heart... Divination could be for you.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The unknowns on my journey...

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Of course, if one wishes to peer into "fate," then hydromancy is the more precise option.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: But that is a complex affair, and to relegate that majestic art to the status of a festive amusement would seem somewhat uncouth. Besides... it is sometimes better to not know "fate" with great certainty.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Hence, I shall use the suitably festive Lunar Arcana to tell your fortune instead. It is more popular with the youth in any case.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Lunar Arcana...

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Indeed. Unlike hydromancy, this will only display possibilities and trends.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: People like think of themselves as creatures of agency and free will. Peering too far and too clearly into the future is detrimental to both body and soul.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I'd like to give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Of course you may. Come then. Take a seat, Miss Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Before we begin... Are there any specific questions you would like to ask?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm... Let's stick to general possibilities and trends, like you suggested.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Ah, very well. Then I shall use the basic Lunar Arcana deck.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Now, try to relax. Cast your mind upon the things you have experienced, and the things you are soon to experience. I will shuffle the deck.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Would you like to the cut the cards yourself?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...You do it.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: No problem. Now then, to make things easier for the seeker — that is to say, you — I shall decipher the cards from your perspective.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Please, draw the first Lunar Arcana. This represents "destiny," and is the foundation for the divination as a whole.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Now, draw your second card. This will stand for the "past," the sum of all your experiences that have come before.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: And now the third Arcana. This is the "present," your interpretation of the current moment.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Finally, the last card. This shall speak of the "future," which... Oh?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm? A... kuuvahki pulse?

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Fascinating. I've never encountered this before in my role as a diviner. Something has exerted an influence upon this card, causing it to leave its designated position.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: What do you make of this, Miss Columbina? Perhaps this is the guiding hand of fate in action.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Of course, if you wish, you can choose to deny the validity of this card and draw the "future" for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...No, it's fine. Let's go with this one.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: A bold decision. I must say, I'm looking forward to the results.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Well then. Let us flip the Lunar Arcana in sequence, and see what emerges.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: First, "destiny." Ah, no surprises here. The card that represents yours is "The Moon."

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The Moon...

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Indeed. The moon can represent the truth at some times, but deception at others. False peace, destructive calamity, and the world-changing power that lies within.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: When the Moon is placed on the destiny tile, it indicates that your destiny is not what it may appear on the surface. Instead, it may yet have a hidden side.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: It symbolizes a journey through the fog, fraught with uncertainty and deception, where one must face inner challenges head on.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I don't understand...

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Haha, patience, my dear. This is but the first card, which serves as a basis for the interpretations that follow. Our divination will only grow clearer from here on out.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Now then. Flip the second card, the one that speaks for the "past."

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Ah, "The Hermit"... but inverted.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Inverted?

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Yes. "The Hermit" symbolizes solitude, introspection, and the pursuit of truth. When inverted, it represents isolation, truth out of reach, and a path that leads one astray.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Combined with "The Moon" as one's destiny, "The Hermit" inverted represents...

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: A choice you made to stand alone in the past. It was a choice made not out of fear or arrogance, but for reasons that others could not perceive.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: You fumbled through the darkness without a guide. But you did not find your way... rather, you went astray — more than once, it would seem.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Is this about how I became Kuutar despite not wishing to become a god? And how I joined the Fatui because I yearned for a place to belong?)

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: I suspect only you know the answer to this question.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: All is not lost. The past is in the past, and so shall it remain. Shall we look into the "present" now?

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Oh my, "The Lovers." One of the most interesting Lunar Arcana.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: What does this one mean?

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: This means that you have had an unprecedented emotional experience. The joy of finding your soul becoming intertwined with that of another... A precious and wonderful thing indeed.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It's true. I've made a lot of friends recently, and they are very good to me. I like them a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: That sounds lovely. I am most delighted for you. "The Lovers" can also represent important decisions, perhaps related to a parting of ways. Now, if I were to guess...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes... My return to the moon...

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: I understand. Parting with friends is never easy, Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: But rest assured, this is not the end of your journey. There is always another story waiting to be told. The "future" always lies ahead.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The "future"...

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Hehe. Well now, it's finally time to flip this most mysterious of cards. Why did it appear? And what does it wish to tell you?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I'm ready.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Very well. Flip this card and see what lies on the other side...

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Miss Barbeloth? What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: ...This card is "Death."

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: That doesn't sound very good.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: It depends on how we interpret it.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: It is true that it can represent an agonizing death, a complete and utter end. But at the same time, it can also represent rebirth.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Do not forget that your destiny card is "The Moon." That lends your future many different potential meanings.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: If death spells the end... is it unavoidable?

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: As I have said, divination can only display general trends. It is a rough guide, but it does not show predetermined outcomes.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Allow me to summarize it for you.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: In the past, you may have lost your way, but now, you have gained new connections and new strength.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: You now face an important decision, one that may bring about a great change in what is yet to be.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: This change might, in turn, be the end of all things... or their beginning.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: But remember, everything is subject to change because of "The Moon" present in your destiny. You must see the truth clearly and face your innermost thoughts.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The truth... my innermost thoughts...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Thank you, Miss Barbeloth.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Don't mention it. Some people dislike divinations, for fear of glimpsing an ending to their story that they wish was not so.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: But I can see that you're different. The result of this divination will not sway your decision.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: This is a rare quality, and one that diviners always hope to see in the seeker. We are here merely to guide, not to exert undue influence.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Go then, and illuminate your future, Miss Columbina. The moonlight that shines from you now is most captivating.

dialogues.speaker: Metta
dialogues.text: But I was aiming right at it...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ah, what a pity. I saw it with my own eyes — you were so close, so, so very close...

dialogues.speaker: Metta
dialogues.text: That's not true! It dodged outta the way right as I was about to snag it!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I'm sorry?

dialogues.speaker: Metta
dialogues.text: You heard me! This paper frog can move! I swear!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Dear, oh dear. What are you saying? How could a paper frog move? Unless you believe there really is magic in this world?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: But even if I, the mere humble merchant that I am, knew such magic, surely I would not use it on a paper frog! I'd sooner give Mora legs, so it could walk right into my purse.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: My dear, dear customer... Why not have one more try, hmm? This time, I'll give you... 12% off! A very generous discount for one of my most regular customers!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Just think about how much experience you have under your belt now! You're sure to win the next one!

dialogues.speaker: Metta
dialogues.text: Um...

dialogues.speaker: Metta
dialogues.text: Darn, I used up all my coins. I'll be right back — just gonna fetch some more from my house!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Take your time! But, uh, don't take too long. This event is Moon-Prayer Night only. Miss it, and you'll have to wait a whole year before I'm back.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Next customer, please. Welcome!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hello.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: (Whoa, whoa, what's this bigwig doing over here!? Ugh, how do I tell my employees not to go running around this time... Shooting them a glance won't work — I haven't known them long enough!)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Dori?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Why hello there, Miss Columbina. Would you like to play my ring-toss game? The rules are very simple, and it's easy to get the hang of...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: How much for a round?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Oh, first time's free! Not a single Mora! After that — well, we can cross that bridge if and when we come to it...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: But with your sharp eye— I mean, sharp skills, I'm sure you'll win all the prizes in one fell swoop!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: (That was an obvious enough hint for them, right? Right...?)

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Let's see now, let's see...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Wow, very good. That's the highest score we've had all night!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ah, what a shame. But practice makes perfect! Another few tries and I'm sure you'll get it.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: And here's your prize. Now, how about another round? As for the cost...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Happy Moon-Prayer Night, Miss Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Happy Moon-Prayer Night, Durin and Hat Guy. Are you here to play the game?

dialogues.speaker: #Durin & {REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: Yes.\nNo.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: No.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You said we were just coming here to say hello...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I did, but then I recognized a few more people as I got closer.

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: (Do my eyes deceive me? Is that...?)

dialogues.speaker: Padisarah
dialogues.text: (It's our little dragon! He's all grown up!)

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Tsk... Someone's popular.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Well now, since you came all this way, why don't you try out this lovely game we have going? First try is free!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: He'll have a go. I'll pass.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Uh... It's only one free try per customer, you can't give your try to him...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I'm aware.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: How has Elder Almond been lately?

dialogues.speaker: Padisarah
dialogues.text: He's in great shape! He goes for a run in the forest every morning to stay fit and healthy.

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: He tried to go boat racing with Firecracker a while back... But he couldn't even make it onto the lotus leaf. Firecracker was in fits of laughter...

dialogues.speaker: Padisarah
dialogues.text: How about you, little dragon? Can you still fly?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Yes, I can.

dialogues.speaker: Padisarah
dialogues.text: But you've become less chatty. Has growing up been tough on you?

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: We call that "maturity." You know, the thing people sing about!

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: "The knight wields a sword of stone, to defend those hearts that are made of gold."

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: Stone is very heavy. That's what keeps him from talking too much.

dialogues.speaker: Padisarah
dialogues.text: That's awesome! I wanna be a knight when I grow up, too! Ring, here I come! Hah!

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: Ah, the hat-wearing man. I never thought I'd see you again. You seem more determined than when I saw you last on the train.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: If you say so.

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: I do say so. The people you once helped see it clearly... it's because you are once again on the right track.

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: May the engine in our hearts propel us to the station of our dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Esnoir
dialogues.text: I can move! I can move now, Rozel!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: (What are they doing, running into the rings like that...!?)

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: You got them all so quickly...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: (I have never seen anything like this in all my travels. Is this guy actually an old friend of theirs?)

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: (But how? They're origami animals and clockwork people from a fairy tale! Getting to know them would be quite an arduous task, unless... they share a hometown?)

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: (Hmm... I have to get to the bottom of this. Next time I see the Great Mage Alice, I shall demand answers!)

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Thank you, Dori. I had a lot of fun.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Heh, so... now for your prize... Hmm, where did I put it? Give me a moment to... dig it out...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: (Ohh, sweet grand prize... How I wish I didn't have to let you go!)

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: (Good thing I've already turned a profit from the customers earlier in the night. Otherwise, I'd have wasted all my hard work...)

dialogues.speaker: Metta
dialogues.text: Okay, *panting* I'm... I'm back!

dialogues.speaker: Metta
dialogues.text: What!? ...I leave for two seconds and someone's already claimed the grand prize!?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ahaha, well, uh... Mm, these things happen, y'know? Perhaps you'd be interested in one of the other prizes instead? We've got all kinds of wonderful goodies here!

dialogues.speaker: Metta
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm... Is this the thing you wanted?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Here, you can have it.

dialogues.speaker: Metta
dialogues.text: Huh? But...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it. It will be happier with you.

dialogues.speaker: Metta
dialogues.text: Thanks so much, Miss! ...Uh, I mean — Moon Goddess!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: (Oh, goodness gracious, Columbina! Give me strength! How am I supposed to make any more money from this child at this rate!?)

dialogues.speaker: Vesa
dialogues.text: Daddy, look! That's the game I was telling you about!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: (*sigh* Forget it. She is the Moon Goddess, after all... I'll think of some other way to swing this. Maybe I can try to hook this new kid...)

dialogues.speaker: Vesa
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh... Someone already won the grand prize...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...You can take mine if you want.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: (Why, why, why? Why are all these bleeding hearts coming here to ruin my business!?)

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Happy Moon Prayer Night, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Happy Moon-Prayer Night.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Well, well, look who it is? I heard someone went and disappeared on us the moment we let her out of our sight. They looked all over for you.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Frankly, I didn't think you'd be back for Moon-Prayer Night.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Were you worried about me, Sandrone?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hah! You'd like that, wouldn't you? Do you even hear what you're saying?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It seems to me like you disguised yourself with festive headgear, just so that you could come see me on Moon-Prayer Night and make sure I'm okay. You didn't even bring Pulonia with you.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You...! I thought you couldn't see!?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I cannot, but I sense the confusion of those around us rippling through the kuuvahki currents.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Based on what I know about you, let me guess what you're wearing. Is it... cat ears?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Shut up! I'm only here to protect the Fatui's interests in this territory. Running into you was pure bad luck!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Really? But you were the one who asked Arlecchino to help everyone find my name...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Columbinaaaa! Just ONE more word, and I'll unscrew your vocal cords!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It's "Columbina Hyposelenia" now.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Tell someone who cares!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I've missed you, Sandrone. The whole time I was gone, I was thinking...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...I hope I get a chance to say some ugly words to you.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Is that supposed to be a joke?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Anyway — let's go play that game.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: What? You mean that Frostfin Whale?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. It's some kind of game where you get bitten if you step on the wrong tooth. Seems like fun.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Who in their right mind would wanna—

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Because you're not a scaredy-cat?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Gah! Fine! You wanna play, let's play! Don't complain when I kick your sorry butt!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Lovely. Ah...

dialogues.speaker: Koski
dialogues.text: You old geezer! I'm gonna beat the pants off you, just you watch!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hehe, I almost forgot. Sandrone?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Mmm? What is it now?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You'd better not lose, or I'm going to beat your head in.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...What!?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Ah! Argh!!!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I think you might have picked a bad tooth, Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Shut it!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Do you need any help? It seems like you're stuck.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: No!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: It's just a blasted... toy... How is its grip this strong!?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Haha...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Stop laughing!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Alright. Well, you lost, so just like I promised...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: H—Hey! What are you doing!? Are you seriously—

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Hyah!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Gah! Why, you— Just you wait!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Rematch!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Are you alright, Sandrone? That was quite a strong bite. Are your clockwork parts...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Quit your fussing. I don't need it!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Alright. I'll go first this time.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (I see it now. She can sense which teeth are rigged.)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (So I just need to avoid the same ones that she does.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: This one... Hmm, seems fine.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (She avoided that one, then? Hmph, now I've got you.)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alright. My turn.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...What!?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Looks like you lost again, Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Wait... There's more than one bad tooth!?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Bonk.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Stupid game! What idiot came up with this!?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Are you alright, Sandrone? You said some nasty things just now.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Oh, I'm peachy.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Should I let you bonk me on the head as well?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Forget it!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Come on, bonk away. It can be your consolation prize. For losing so badly.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I told you, forget it!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Gah, you've always been so annoying...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Singing right outside my door, inviting yourself to my tea parties, going AWOL... and now you're off to the moon, or something!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Of all my days with the Fatui... The times I spent with you, Arlecchino, and Rosalyne... They were my favorite.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I will not forget them, just as I shall not forget this moment.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: We'll always be friends, no matter where we are, right?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Who'd want to be your...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I'll miss you, Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Goodbye, Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I'll... miss you too... Columbina...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry? What was that?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Waah!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waaah! Yeesh, no need to freak out... What's wrong? We've been looking everywhere for you.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: What do you want!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Whoa, nice ears...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: What... do... you... WANT!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, uh... th—this...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: ...Huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's your turn to draw something. You're one of her friends too, aren't you?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Hmph. Doesn't know how lucky she is...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Sorry?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Nothing. I'm done. Take it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That was fast!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and one more thing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Last time we spoke, you mentioned you were interested in the Narzissenkreuz Ordo's research. Remember? There were too many people when we last met, so we didn't get the chance to do this.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: What are you talking about?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'd like you have a look at this...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: This is— Oh... Alain, Rene... and Mary-Ann...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And this.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Huh... The Holy Blade... A savior's plaything.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You don't approve of their goals?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: It's not about whether I approve or not.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: These people... They would sacrifice themselves for the sake of the world — especially Alain Guillotin and Rene.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: That is something I would never choose to do.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Still... Heh. I didn't know they had any pictures left from that time.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: If I'd thought to bring a Kamera, I'd have...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's okay. We snapped a photo.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: ...What!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, of you being bitten by the Frostfin Whale, and Columbina bonking you on the head.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Tear it up! NOW!!!

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: Moon-Prayer Candy! Beautiful, tasty Moon-Prayer Candy! Buy a whole box, share it with your friends and family!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Candy... to share? ...Hmm, I wonder what flavors everyone would like...)

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: Welcome home, Moon Goddess! Fancy a box of Moon-Prayer Candy?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: I knew you would! Now, what flavor would you like?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I'm not sure... what flavors do you have?

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: Is this for yourself, or as a gift?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: A gift for my friends.

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: Ah, I see. In that case, I'd recommend Apple, Lakkaberry , or Midsommar Berry. Those are the most popular.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Do you have Nocturnal Blossom flavor?

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: Huh. I've seen couples give those as gifts before, but I did not know they were edible...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: No? Okay, then... Moonfall Silver?

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: Uhhh... You did say this was for friends, right?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Um... Maybe Smetana, then?

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: Hey, now that's a creative idea... I've never tried it before, but if you're happy to wait, I can see about whipping up a batch on the spot.

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: While we're at it... you got any other ideas?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Green grass. Krumkake. Extra-strong coffee. Columbina describes the flavors that come to mind.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The scent of exotic candy soon draws over the nearby children, who excited form a line. Before long, everyone is brainstorming new ideas for flavors...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Smoked Fish Steak. Berries and Fried Meat. Rain-soaked Moon-Prayer Blossom.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The stall owner, peppered with expectant gazes on every side, lets his courage soar free, and colorful candies are placed in the box one after another.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: This feels like... the surprise of my life.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you like it?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I do. I never imagined I'd ever get to enjoy Moon-Prayer Night with everyone so freely...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, if you're happy, we're happy!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Quite a strategy you came up with — hide the tree in the forest... It's not your usual style, Lauma. Is there something about Moon-Prayer Night that enhances what's in your head as well as the antlers on top?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Apparently so. It even inspired a perennial penny pincher to use their resources for a greater cause. It truly is a magical festival.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (I see it now. This bickering is actually a sign of a strong relationship.)

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Huh? What's everyone doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Oh! Miss Columbina! You're back!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. I'm fine now... thanks for your concern.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How's your progress with Alice's assignment?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Very well indeed. I've never heard her sound so excited.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Isn't she always quite excitable?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Not like this... This time, her excitement seems more serious. Seems like she's had a major breakthrough.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: She said she'll contact us once she knows more. In the meantime, we're free to relax and have some fun.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Enjoy the time off while it lasts. I have a feeling that our next task won't be so simple.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Mm... I should go. I still have a few things to attend to at the Frostmoon Scions' stall.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: And I think I'll take a look around. With any luck, this once-in-a-year festival will come with once-in-a-year opportunities.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold up a second, where's Varka?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I believe he made a beeline for The Flagship the moment he entered Nasha Town.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah. That's Mondstadters for you — they know what they want when festivals roll around...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Goodbye for now, Columbina. I hope you have a wonderful night.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I will.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, well in that case, don't just stand there — get out there and have some fun! You'll definitely get a warm welcome at every stall!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, also — take this map with you. It's a guide to the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Frostmoon Scions' stall is over here. Lauma's invited a whole bunch of cute animals to celebrate too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Over there is the Hexenzirkel section. Alice seemed more excited than anyone about this festival, so she insisted on making it a grand affair.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and then there's the Nasha Town local specialties, including... actually, forget that, better if you go check them out for yourself!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Thank you. It looks like a lot of fun.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Enjoy your Moon-Prayer Night.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You're not coming with me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'll be around! But don't you wanna browse by yourself for a bit first?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Um...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup! If you find something you like and wanna try it out together, just give us a shout — we'll be right with you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Otherwise, just relax and enjoy yourself! There's so much on offer, so try to experience as much as you can... and don't forget to stuff yourself with all the delicious festival food!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll probably run into each other while we're browsing.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Haha. Alright, then... Off I go.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Have fun!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, Columbina! Are you done checking out the festive amusements already?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you sure you don't wanna look around some more? You might not get another opportunity like this for a while...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Right now, what I'd like to do is...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (...Actually, I'd like to have a bit more fun.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You're right... I'm not ready for this night to end just yet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's the spirit! Take your time, Columbina. The most important thing is to have no regrets!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'll be right here if you need us!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Okay, thank you.

talks.objective: Continue enjoying Moon-Prayer Night, or talk to Paimon

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Columbina! Finished with the festival already?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (...Actually, I'd like to have a bit more fun.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay! No need to rush, just take it easy.

talks.objective: Continue enjoying Moon-Prayer Night, or talk to Paimon

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: This was the most fun I've ever had on a Moon-Prayer Night.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Everywhere I went, people were saying "welcome home." And there were friends at every turn.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I only wish it could last longer than one night.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Your friends will always be here.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. You're right. I...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Ah, the Moon-Prayer Blossoms...

dialogues.speaker: Kaarina
dialogues.text: Ooh, look, look!

dialogues.speaker: Lemetti
dialogues.text: Moon-Prayer Night is here!

dialogues.speaker: Reetta
dialogues.text: The moon... It's so beautiful...

dialogues.speaker: Domovoj
dialogues.text: Happy Moon-Prayer Night, dear.

dialogues.speaker: Lyylikki
dialogues.text: Happy Moon-Prayer Night!

dialogues.speaker: Kantor
dialogues.text: Happy Moon-Prayer Night.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Time flies when you're having fun...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Looks like the time has come.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Columbina...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: You'll be... heading off now?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes... To the ruins you mentioned. And from there... back home to the moon.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: ...Wait!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aino?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: At least... at least...!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Take one of our Craftshop's krumkakes up to the moon with you... Y'know, for a snack!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Haha... Sure. Why not?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The Curatorium of Secrets believes in proper farewells. No story should be left without a satisfactory end note.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Nefer...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Farewells are an important affair for the Ratniki, too. We never know when we might meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha... And here I thought grand farewells wouldn't suit tonight's mood. But I suppose friendly passion is not to be stopped, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, we made a little something for you, Columbina!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tada!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh no...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A Moon-Prayer Night greeting card — with drawings by all of your friends.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You did mention that you'd like a portrait done, so I took the liberty of creating one for you.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I, meanwhile, did the portrait of Mr. Albedo, and Mr. Varka did the same for me.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I mean, I think my work was pretty true to life, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The picture of Ashru was my doing. The two of you seemed to get along rather well.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Wait, was I the only one who did a full-body picture? Ugh... That's so embarrassing...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: I did the pictures of me and Ineffa!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I did my own portrait and one for Hat Guy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Plus, there's the two mages, Arlecchino, and Sandrone... So if you ever miss us, just flip the card open, and we'll all be right there with ya!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I don't know what to say... Thank you so much, everyone... This whole Moon-Prayer Night was more than I could've ever asked for... It is the greatest gift I have ever received.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Ah! Lauma. I've figured it out.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Hmm? Figured what out...?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Remember how the Frostmoon Scions used to use milk as invisible ink to write hidden messages?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: That was a very long time ago... Oh! Are you saying...?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. When I miss you all, I shall use moonlight in the same way, to write words that only you can see upon the moon itself.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Wow! That sounds lovely.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Quite, but... How will we see them...?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Simply open your windows on nights when the moon shines bright, and the moonlight will naturally flow towards the words I have written.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: That sounds most fitting indeed. Very true to form.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I'll... try to write them in places that won't disturb your sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I, for one, would sleep all the better for having read one of your messages before settling down for the night.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! So don't worry about disturbing anyone's sleep. Just promise you'll write to let us know you're okay, alright?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Alright, I promise.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: In that case... Columbina, are you ready?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I'm ready.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Very well. Let's go.

choices.text: I'll stay with you to the end.

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: Here you go. Every flavor you asked for is in there!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: Haha, I should be the one thanking you! You brought me a whole bunch of new business! Hehe, it's like a genuine blessing from the Moon Goddess!

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: I hope you and your friends have a lovely night.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: This doesn't make any sense! How am I losing every single time!? ...Wait, Ineffa! You're cheating, aren't you? Yeah, that must be it!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I am not cheating, Aino.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Uh-oh, sounds like Ineffa's turned into a big baloney-bot! I think it's time for some serious maintenance!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Ah. Moon Goddess. Help me...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Miss Columbina, Aino is attempting to cheat—

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: What the...!? I'm not the cheater, you're the cheater! How dare you throw it back at me!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Pfft... Hehehe.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: ...Alright, fine! Let's all laugh at Aino! Just wait till I get home, 'cause I'm gonna make a game bot that can win one hundred percent of the time!

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Let's see you laugh when I come back and beat your butts! Hmph, you'll all have your heads covered in stickers when I'm through with you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We came to check everything was okay after all that yelling... But, uh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pfft... hahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you playing?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Whatever it is, it sounds like cheating is allowed.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Kuuhenki Concentration.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
